audit_notes: Model: steady 1D roof conduction with linearised sol-air boundary; the electrostatic mechanism enters only through the assumed aged reflectance loss, so the simulation checks the thermal consequence of that assumption, not the electrostatics. Checks: ATO at 7 vol% above percolation gives surface resistivity ~1e6-1e9 Ohm/sq and charge relaxation times of seconds, so tribo-charge is removed. However, the soiling that darkens cool roofs is dominated by fine black carbon, organics and biofilm held by van der Waals and capillary forces (adhesion of a 1 um particle ~100 nN vs electrostatic image force ~1 nN for typical charges); electrostatic adhesion matters mostly for coarse (>10 um) mineral grains, which are bright and scatter anyway. I therefore reduce the claimed improvement: aged loss 0.16 instead of 0.15 (baseline 0.18). ATO also absorbs in the NIR, so clean SR 0.84 is kept. Hand result: design alpha = 0.16 + 0.16 = 0.32 -> q = 0.5*(96 + 150 - 76.5)/15.5 = 5.47 W/m2 vs 5.56 W/m2: ~-2 %. Dimensionless: ratio electrostatic to van der Waals adhesion for 1 um particles ~0.01. No structural concerns beyond the acrylic binder itself (repaint every ~10 years as the baseline). Simulation coefficient: U_eff = 0.484 W/m2K.
